sentences.chinese: 大司農曹莫不署名，季龍使張豺問其故。
sentences.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Cao Mo did not affix his signature; Jilong sent Zhang Chao to ask him the reason.
sentences.idiomatic: When Grand Minister of Agriculture Cao Mo withheld his signature, Shi Hu—Jilong—dispatched Zhang Chao to demand an explanation.

sentences.chinese: 莫頓首曰：「天下業重，不宜立少，是以不敢署也。
sentences.literal: Mo knocked his head on the ground and said: "The enterprise of All-under-Heaven is weighty; it is not fitting to establish the young; therefore I dare not sign."
sentences.idiomatic: Cao Mo kowtowed and answered, "The realm is too heavy a burden to lay on a child—that is why I could not put my name to the deed."

sentences.chinese: 」季龍曰：「莫，忠臣也，然未達朕意。
sentences.literal: " Jilong said: "Mo is a loyal subject, yet he has not grasped Our intention."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu replied, "Cao Mo is a faithful minister; he simply does not see what I mean."

sentences.chinese: 張舉、李農知吾心矣，其令諭之。
sentences.literal: Zhang Ju and Li Nong know Our mind; order them to explain it to him."
sentences.idiomatic: "Zhang Ju and Li Nong already understand my purpose—have them make it clear to him."

sentences.chinese: 」遂立世為皇太子，劉氏為皇后。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he established Shi as heir apparent and the Liu clan woman as empress.
sentences.idiomatic: He then named Shi Shi crown prince and invested Lady Liu as empress.

sentences.chinese: 季龍召太常條攸、光祿勳杜嘏謂之曰：「煩卿傅太子，實希改轍，吾之相托，卿宜明之。
sentences.literal: Jilong summoned Grand Master of Ceremonies Tiao You and Superintendent of the Household Du Gu and said to them: "We trouble you two to tutor the heir; We truly hope for a change of course; as for Our entrusting this matter to you, you ought to understand it clearly."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu called in Tiao You, grand master of ceremonies, and Du Gu, superintendent of the household, and told them, "I ask you to instruct the heir and truly wish him to mend his ways; what I am handing you, you must take to heart."

sentences.chinese: 」署攸太傅，嘏為少傅。
sentences.literal: " He appointed You grand tutor and Gu junior tutor.
sentences.idiomatic: He named Tiao You grand tutor and Du Gu junior tutor to the heir.

sentences.chinese: 季龍時疾瘳，以僭即皇帝位於南郊，大赦境內，建元曰太寧。
sentences.literal: When at that time Jilong's illness had abated, he usurped the imperial title at the southern suburb, granted a general amnesty within the borders, and established the era name Great Tranquility.
sentences.idiomatic: Once Shi Hu had rallied from his sickness, he arrogated the throne at the southern suburban altar, proclaimed an empire-wide amnesty, and adopted the reign title Tauning.

sentences.chinese: 百官增位一等，諸子進爵郡王。
sentences.literal: All officials had their positions raised one grade; his various sons were advanced in noble rank to princes of commanderies.
sentences.idiomatic: Every minister gained a step in rank, and his sons were promoted to princes of commanderies.

sentences.chinese: 以尚書張良為右僕射。
sentences.literal: He appointed Masters-of-Writing Zhang Liang as right vice-director.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Liang of the secretariat was made right vice-director.

sentences.chinese: 故東宮謫卒高力等萬餘人當戍涼州，行達雍城，既不在赦例，又敕雍州刺史張茂送之。
sentences.literal: Former eastern-palace degraded soldiers called the Gao Li, more than ten thousand men, were due to be garrisoned in Liangzhou; en route they reached Yongcheng; they were not within the categories of amnesty, and moreover an edict ordered Yongzhou Governor Zhang Mao to escort them on.
sentences.idiomatic: Over ten thousand demoted eastern-palace toughs known as the Gao Li were bound for Liangzhou; when they reached Yongcheng they fell outside the amnesty, and the throne ordered Governor Zhang Mao to march them onward.

sentences.chinese: 茂皆奪其馬，令步推鹿車，致糧戍所。
sentences.literal: Mao seized all their horses, ordered them to go on foot pushing deer carts, and had grain delivered to the garrison place.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Mao confiscated their mounts and made them haul supplies on foot in handcarts all the way to the posting.

sentences.chinese: 高力督定陽梁犢等害眾心之怨，謀起兵東還，陰令胡人頡獨鹿微告戍者，戍者皆踴抃大呼。
sentences.literal: Gao Li supervisor Liang Du of Dingyang and others nursed the resentment boiling in every breast, plotted to raise troops and return east, secretly ordered the Hu man Xiedulu to hint to the garrison men, and the garrison men all leaped, clapped, and shouted.
sentences.idiomatic: Their overseer Liang Du of Dingyang and his comrades, burning with the men's grievances, plotted an eastern mutiny; Xiedulu quietly tipped off the conscripts, who burst into cheers and stamped their approval.

sentences.chinese: 梁犢乃自稱晉征東大將軍，率眾攻陷下辯，逼張茂為大都督、大司馬，載以軺車。
sentences.literal: Liang Du then styled himself Jin's General Who Conquers the East, led the host to storm and take Xiabian, compelled Zhang Mao to become grand commander-in-chief and grand marshal, and conveyed him in a light carriage.
sentences.idiomatic: Liang Du declared himself Jin's eastern-expedition commander, seized Xiabian, forced Zhang Mao to take the titles of grand commander and grand marshal, and paraded him in an open coach.

sentences.chinese: 安西劉甯自安定擊之，大敗而還。
sentences.literal: Anxi Liu Ning struck them from Anding and was greatly defeated and returned.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Ning, the western pacifier, attacked from Anding and limped back in rout.

sentences.chinese: 秦、雍間城戍無不摧陷，斬二千石長史，長驅而東。
sentences.literal: Between Qin and Yong no city garrison failed to be shattered; they beheaded administrators of two-thousand-shi salary rank and drove straight east.
sentences.idiomatic: Fort after fort between Qin and Yong fell; they slew salary-rank governors and swept eastward without pause.

sentences.chinese: 高力等皆多力善射，一當十餘人，雖無兵甲，所在掠百姓大斧，施一丈柯，攻戰若神，所向崩潰，戍卒皆隨之，比至長安，眾已十萬。
sentences.literal: The Gao Li and their like were all strong of arm and skilled at archery; one man matched more than ten; though they lacked armor and weapons, wherever they went they plundered the common people's great axes, fitted shafts of one zhang, fought as if divine, and wherever they aimed lines collapsed; garrison troops all followed them; by the time they reached Chang'an, the host already numbered one hundred thousand.
sentences.idiomatic: Those Gao Li fighters were archers and brawlers who could each hold off a dozen men; unarmed, they seized farmers' broadaxes, mounted them on ten-foot helves, and swept through defenses like spirits until every garrison joined them—by Chang'an their horde had swollen to a hundred thousand.

sentences.chinese: 其樂平王石苞時鎮長安，盡銳距之，一戰而敗。
sentences.literal: Prince of Leping Shi Bao at that time was stationed at Chang'an; he committed his sharpest troops to resisting them and was defeated in one battle.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Bao, prince of Leping, held Chang'an and threw his best troops against the rebels, only to lose at the first clash.

sentences.chinese: 犢遂東出潼關，進如洛川。
sentences.literal: Liang Du then went east out of Tong Pass and advanced toward the Luochuan region.
sentences.idiomatic: Liang Du broke east through Tong Pass and rolled on toward the Luoyang basin.

sentences.chinese: 季龍以李農為大都督，行大將軍事，統衛軍張賀度、征西張良、征虜石閔等，率步騎十萬討之。
sentences.literal: Jilong appointed Li Nong as grand commander-in-chief, acting grand general's duties, commanding guards-army Zhang Hedu, western campaign Zhang Liang, captive-quelling Shi Min, and others, and led one hundred thousand infantry and horse to punish them.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu named Li Nong commander-in-chief with plenipotentiary general's powers, put Zhang Hedu, Zhang Liang, Shi Min, and others under him, and sent a hundred thousand horse and foot to crush the rising.

sentences.chinese: 戰于新安，農師不利。
sentences.literal: They fought at Xin'an; Li Nong's army fared ill.
sentences.idiomatic: Battle joined at Xin'an, and Li Nong's line buckled.

sentences.chinese: 又戰于洛陽，農師又敗，乃退壁成皋。
sentences.literal: Again they fought at Luoyang; Li Nong's army was again defeated; thereupon he withdrew and fortified at Chenggao.
sentences.idiomatic: A second clash at Luoyang broke him again, so he pulled back and dug in at Chenggao.

sentences.chinese: 犢東掠滎陽、陳留諸郡，季龍大懼，以燕王石斌為大都督中外諸軍事，率精騎一萬，統姚弋仲、苻洪等擊犢于滎陽東，大敗之，斬犢首而還，討其餘黨，盡滅之。
sentences.literal: Liang Du raided east through Xingyang, Chenliu, and the various commanderies; Jilong was greatly afraid; he appointed Prince of Yan Shi Bin as grand commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without, led ten thousand picked cavalry, commanded Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, and others, and struck Liang Du east of Xingyang, greatly defeated him, beheaded Liang Du and returned, punished his remaining faction, and utterly extinguished them.
sentences.idiomatic: As Liang Du pillaged Xingyang and Chenliu, Shi Hu panicked; he gave Shi Bin, prince of Yan, supreme command, ten thousand elite riders, and lieutenants Yao Yizhong and Fu Hong, shattered Liang Du east of Xingyang, brought back his head, and extirpated the rest of his party.

sentences.chinese: 俄而晉將軍王龕拔其沛郡。
sentences.literal: Before long Jin general Wang Kan captured their Pei commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin's Wang Kan ripped Pei commandery from Zhao hands.

sentences.chinese: 始平人馬勖起兵于洛氏葛谷，自稱將軍。
sentences.literal: A man of Shiping, Ma Xu, raised troops at Luoshi Ge Valley and styled himself general.
sentences.idiomatic: Ma Xu of Shiping rose in Luoshi Ge Valley and proclaimed himself a general.

sentences.chinese: 石苞攻滅之，誅三千餘家。
sentences.literal: Shi Bao attacked and destroyed him, executing more than three thousand households.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Bao stamped out the band and put over three thousand households to the sword.

sentences.chinese: 時熒惑犯積屍，又犯昴、月，及熒惑北犯河鼓。
sentences.literal: At that time Mars encroached on the Pile of Corpses asterism, also encroached on Mao and the moon, and Mars went north to encroach on River Drum.
sentences.idiomatic: Heaven sent Mars across the Pile of Corpses, across the Pleiades and the moon, and north toward the River Drum stars—a grim sky.

sentences.chinese: 未幾，季龍疾甚，以石遵為大將軍，鎮關右，石斌為丞相、錄尚書事，張豺為鎮衛大將軍、領軍將軍、吏部尚書，並受遺輔政。
sentences.literal: Before long Jilong's illness was severe; he appointed Shi Zun as grand general guarding the land west of the passes, Shi Bin as chancellor and recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, Zhang Chao as grand general who guards the realm, commanding-general of the army, and minister of personnel, all receiving testamentary mandate to assist rule.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu soon sank mortally ill; he named Shi Zun grand general for the Guanzhong west, Shi Bin chancellor with custody of the secretariat, and Zhang Chao capital guardian, army commander, and personnel minister—each charged by deathbed edict to steer the state.

sentences.chinese: 劉氏懼斌之輔政也害世，與張豺謀誅之。
sentences.literal: Lady Liu feared that if Bin assisted rule he would harm Shi; she plotted with Zhang Chao to execute him.
sentences.idiomatic: Empress Liu feared Shi Bin as regent would murder young Shi Shi; she conspired with Zhang Chao to kill him first.

sentences.chinese: 斌時在襄國，乃遣使詐斌曰：「主上患已漸損，王須獵者，可小停也。
sentences.literal: Bin was at Xiangguo; she then sent an envoy falsely telling Bin: "The sovereign's ailment has gradually lessened; if the king needs hunting, he may pause a little."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Bin was in Xiangguo; she sent a messenger with a lie: "The emperor is mending; if you mean to hunt, you may linger awhile."

sentences.chinese: 」斌性好酒耽獵，遂遊畋縱飲。
sentences.literal: Bin by nature loved wine and was addicted to hunting; thereupon he roamed hunting and drank without restraint.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Bin loved wine and the chase; he gave himself to hunts and drinking binges.

sentences.chinese: 劉氏矯命稱斌無忠孝之心，免斌官，以王歸第，使張豺弟雄率龍騰五百人守之。
sentences.literal: Lady Liu forged orders saying Bin lacked loyal and filial heart, dismissed Bin from office, ordered him as a prince to return to his mansion, and sent Zhang Chao's brother Zhang Xiong leading five hundred Dragon Surge troops to guard him.
sentences.idiomatic: She forged an edict accusing Shi Bin of disloyalty, stripped his offices, sent the prince home under house arrest, and posted Zhang Xiong with five hundred Dragon Surge guards.

sentences.chinese: 石遵自幽州至鄴，敕朝堂受拜，配禁兵三萬遣之，遵慟泣而去。
sentences.literal: Shi Zun came from Youzhou to Ye; he was ordered to receive appointment at the court hall, was allotted thirty thousand palace guards and dispatched; Zun wept bitterly and departed.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Zun rode from Youzhou to Ye, was made to take his commission in open court, handed thirty thousand household troops, and sent away weeping.

sentences.chinese: 是日季龍疾小瘳，問曰：「遵至未？
sentences.literal: That day Jilong's illness slightly abated; he asked: "Has Zun arrived?"
sentences.idiomatic: That same day Shi Hu briefly rallied and asked, "Has Shi Zun come?"

sentences.chinese: 」左右答言久已去矣。
sentences.literal: " Those at his side answered that long ago he had already gone.
sentences.idiomatic: His attendants said he had left long since.

sentences.chinese: 季龍曰：「恨不見之。
sentences.literal: Jilong said: "We regret not having seen him."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu murmured, "How I wish I could have seen him."

sentences.chinese: 」季龍臨於西閣，龍騰將軍、中郎二百餘人列拜於前。
sentences.literal: " Jilong attended at the western gallery; more than two hundred Dragon Surge generals and gentlemen-of-the-household lined up and bowed before him.
sentences.idiomatic: He received them at the western gallery, where over two hundred Dragon Surge officers and household gentlemen bowed in ranks.

sentences.chinese: 季龍曰：「何所求也？
sentences.literal: Jilong said: "What do you seek?"
sentences.idiomatic: "What do you want of me?" he asked.

sentences.chinese: 」皆言聖躬不和，宜令燕王入宿衛，典兵馬，或言乞為皇太子。
sentences.literal: " They all said the sacred person was unwell; Yan Wang ought to enter to guard overnight and command troops and horses; some begged to become crown prince.
sentences.idiomatic: They pleaded that the sovereign was failing and the prince of Yan should enter to command the guard; others clamored to be named heir.

sentences.chinese: 季龍不知斌之廢也，責曰：「燕王不在內邪？
sentences.literal: Jilong did not know Bin had been dismissed; he rebuked them, saying: "Is not the Prince of Yan within?"
sentences.idiomatic: Unaware Shi Bin had been cashiered, Shi Hu snapped, "Is not the prince of Yan already inside?"

sentences.chinese: 呼來！
sentences.literal: Call him here!"
sentences.idiomatic: "Summon him at once!"

sentences.chinese: 」左右言王酒病，不能入。
sentences.literal: " Those at his side said the king was ill from wine and could not enter.
sentences.idiomatic: They answered that the prince was drunk-sick and could not come.

sentences.chinese: 季龍曰：「促持輦迎之，當付其璽綬。
sentences.literal: Jilong said: "Hurry—take a palanquin to welcome him; We shall hand him the seals and cords."
sentences.idiomatic: "Send a litter—quickly," Shi Hu ordered. "I will give him the seals myself."

sentences.chinese: 」亦竟無行者。
sentences.literal: " Yet in the end none went.
sentences.idiomatic: No one moved to obey.

sentences.chinese: 尋昏眩而入。
sentences.literal: Shortly he entered in dizziness.
sentences.idiomatic: Moments later he collapsed into a stupor.

sentences.chinese: 張豺使弟雄等矯季龍命殺斌，劉氏又矯命以豺為太保、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，加千兵百騎，一依霍光輔漢故事。
sentences.literal: Zhang Chao had his brother Xiong and others forge Jilong's order to kill Bin; Lady Liu again forged orders appointing Zhang Chao grand guardian, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, adding a thousand infantry and hundred horse in guard, entirely according to the precedent of Huo Guang assisting Han.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Chao's brother Xiong forged an order executing Shi Bin; Liu forged another elevating Zhang Chao to grand guardian, supreme commander, and secretariat overseer with a thousand foot and a hundred horse—aping Huo Guang's regency over Han.

sentences.chinese: 侍中徐統歎曰：「禍將作矣，吾無為豫之。
sentences.literal: Attendant-in-chief Xu Tong sighed: "Calamity is about to arise; I will not put myself among those who prepare for it beforehand."
sentences.idiomatic: Palace attendant Xu Tong groaned, "The storm is coming—I want no part of the schemes ahead."

sentences.chinese: 」乃仰藥而死。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he drank poison and died.
sentences.idiomatic: He swallowed poison and died.

sentences.chinese: 俄而季龍亦死。
sentences.literal: Before long Jilong also died.
sentences.idiomatic: Soon Shi Hu followed him to the grave.

sentences.chinese: 季龍始以僭立，至此，凡在位十五歲。
sentences.literal: Jilong had begun by usurping the throne; reaching this point, altogether he had occupied the throne fifteen years.
sentences.idiomatic: From his seizure of the throne to this hour Shi Hu had reigned fifteen years.

sentences.chinese: 石世
sentences.literal: Shi Shi.
sentences.idiomatic: Section heading: the boy emperor Shi Shi.

sentences.chinese: 於是世即偽位，尊劉氏為皇太后，臨朝，進張豺為丞相。
sentences.literal: Thereupon Shi succeeded to the false throne, honored Lady Liu as empress dowager with court regency, and advanced Zhang Chao to chancellor.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Shi mounted the puppet throne, raised Lady Liu to ruling empress dowager, and made Zhang Chao chancellor.

sentences.chinese: 豺請石遵、石鑒為左右丞相，以尉其心，劉氏從之。
sentences.literal: Zhang Chao requested Shi Zun and Shi Jian as left and right chancellors to soothe their hearts; Lady Liu followed this.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Chao named Shi Zun and Shi Jian left and right chancellors to buy their loyalty; Liu agreed.

sentences.chinese: 豺與張舉謀誅李農，而舉與農素善，以豺謀告之。
sentences.literal: Zhang Chao plotted with Zhang Ju to kill Li Nong, but Zhang Ju was on good terms with Li Nong and informed Li Nong of Zhang Chao's plot.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Chao and Zhang Ju planned Li Nong's murder, yet Zhang Ju, Li Nong's friend, leaked the plot.

sentences.chinese: 農懼，率騎百餘奔廣宗，率乞活數萬家保于上白。
sentences.literal: Li Nong feared, led more than a hundred horsemen and fled to Guangzong, and led several tens of thousands of Qiehuo households to hold Shangbai.
sentences.idiomatic: Terrified, Li Nong galloped to Guangzong with a hundred riders and rallied tens of thousands of Qiehuo refugee families on Mount Shangbai.

sentences.chinese: 劉氏使張舉等統宿衛精卒圍之。
sentences.literal: Lady Liu sent Zhang Ju and others to command elite palace-guard troops to besiege them.
sentences.idiomatic: Lady Liu dispatched Zhang Ju with the household elite to invest the mountain.

sentences.chinese: 豺以張離為鎮軍大將軍、監中外諸軍事、司隸校尉，為己之副。
sentences.literal: Zhang Chao appointed Zhang Li as grand general who stabilizes the army, overseer of all military affairs within and without, metropolitan governor, as his own deputy.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Chao made Zhang Li army-stabilizing commander, overseer of all forces, metropolitan governor, and his second-in-command.

sentences.chinese: 鄴中群盜大起，迭相劫掠。
sentences.literal: In Ye bandits arose in great numbers, repeatedly raiding one another.
sentences.idiomatic: Ye erupted in robbery as gangs preyed on one another.

sentences.chinese: 石遵聞季龍之死，屯於河內。
sentences.literal: When Shi Zun heard of Jilong's death, he encamped at Henei.
sentences.idiomatic: Learning of Shi Hu's death, Shi Zun halted his army at Henei.

sentences.chinese: 姚弋仲、苻洪、石閔、劉甯及武衛王鸞、甯西王午、石榮、王鐵、立義將軍段勤等既平秦、洛，班師而歸，遇遵于李城，說遵曰：「殿下長而且賢，先帝亦有意于殿下矣。
sentences.literal: Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, Shi Min, Liu Ning, and martial guard Wang Luan, western pacification Wang Wu, Shi Rong, Wang Tie, righteous-establishment general Duan Qin and others, having pacified Qin and Luo, rotated the army home, met Zun at Licheng, and urged Zun, saying: "Your Highness is eldest and worthy; the late emperor also had intentions toward Your Highness.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, Shi Min, Liu Ning, Wang Luan of the martial guard, Wang Wu of western pacification, Shi Rong, Wang Tie, Duan Qin the righteous-establishment general, and the rest—fresh from pacifying Qin and Luoyang—ran into Shi Zun at Licheng and pleaded, "You are the eldest worthy prince; the late emperor already favored you.

sentences.chinese: 但以末年惛惑，為張豺所誤。
sentences.literal: Only because in his closing years he was muddled and deluded was he misled by Zhang Chao.
sentences.idiomatic: Only his final confusion let Zhang Chao lead him astray."

sentences.chinese: 今上白相持未下，京師宿衛空虛，若聲張豺之罪，鼓行而討之，孰不倒戈開門而迎殿下者邪！
sentences.literal: Now Shangbai still stalemates unconquered; the capital's palace guard stands empty; if we proclaim Zhang Chao's crimes and march with drums beating to punish him, who would not turn halberds and open gates to welcome Your Highness!"
sentences.idiomatic: Shangbai still holds out and the capital guard is hollow—denounce Zhang Chao and march in formation, and every soldier will drop his weapon and throw open the gates for you!"

sentences.chinese: 」遵從之。
sentences.literal: Zun followed this.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Zun took their counsel.

sentences.chinese: 洛州刺史劉國等亦率洛陽之眾至於李城。
sentences.literal: Luozhou Governor Liu Guo and others also led Luoyang's host and arrived at Licheng.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Guo, governor of Luozhou, marched the Luoyang garrison to join them at Licheng.

sentences.chinese: 遵檄至鄴，張豺大懼，馳召上白之軍。
sentences.literal: When Zun's proclamation reached Ye, Zhang Chao was greatly afraid and urgently recalled the army at Shangbai.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Chao panicked when Shi Zun's manifesto hit Ye and frantically pulled the Shangbai siege army home.

sentences.chinese: 遵次於蕩陰，戎卒九萬，石閔為前鋒。
sentences.literal: Zun halted at Dangyin; field troops numbered ninety thousand; Shi Min was vanguard.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Zun camped at Dangyin with ninety thousand veterans and Shi Min spearheading the column.

sentences.chinese: 豺將出距之，耆舊羯士皆曰：「天子兒來奔喪，吾當出迎之，不能為張豺城戍也。
sentences.literal: When Zhang Chao was about to go out to resist them, the elderly Jie warriors all said: "The Son of Heaven's son has come to mourn the funeral; we ought to go out to welcome him; we cannot be wall-and-garrison men for Zhang Chao."
sentences.idiomatic: As Zhang Chao prepared to meet them in the field, gray-haired Jie soldiers shouted, "The emperor's son rides to bury his father—we should welcome him, not man Zhang Chao's ramparts."

sentences.chinese: 」逾城而出，豺斬之不能止。
sentences.literal: " They climbed over the walls and went out; Zhang Chao executed them but could not stop it.
sentences.idiomatic: They scaled the walls to desert; Zhang Chao slaughtered them but could not stem the tide.

sentences.chinese: 張離率龍騰二千斬關迎遵。
sentences.literal: Zhang Li led two thousand Dragon Surge troops to cut through the barrier and welcome Zun.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Li smashed a gate with two thousand Dragon Surge troops and ushered Shi Zun inside.

sentences.chinese: 劉氏懼，引張豺入，對之悲哭曰：「先帝梓宮未殯，而禍難繁興。
sentences.literal: Lady Liu feared, led Zhang Chao in, and wept miserably to him, saying: "The late emperor's catafalque has not yet been buried, yet disasters multiply and arise.
sentences.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, Lady Liu drew Zhang Chao in and sobbed, "The late ruler still lies unburied while calamities pile up.

sentences.chinese: 今皇嗣沖幼，托之于將軍，將軍何以匡濟邪？
sentences.literal: Now the imperial heir is young and tender; We entrust him to you, general—how will you rescue and aid?"
sentences.idiomatic: The boy on the throne is helpless—I lean on you, general—how will you save us?"

sentences.chinese: 加遵重官，可以弭不？
sentences.literal: Add Zun high office—can it quell this?"
sentences.idiomatic: Would stacking honors on Shi Zun quiet this storm?"

sentences.chinese: 」豺惶怖失守，無復籌計，但言唯唯。
sentences.literal: " Zhang Chao was panic-stricken and lost his guard, had no further schemes, and only said yes-yes.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Chao went blank with fright, offered no plan, and muttered empty assent.

sentences.chinese: 劉氏令以遵為丞相、領大司馬、大都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，加黃鉞、九錫，增封十郡，委以阿衡之任。
sentences.literal: Lady Liu ordered Zun appointed chancellor, concurrently grand marshal, grand commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, adding golden battle-axe and nine bestowals, increasing fief by ten commanderies, entrusting him with the burden of prime minister like Yi Yin.
sentences.idiomatic: She ordered Shi Zun made chancellor, grand marshal, supreme commander, secretariat overseer, golden-axe bearer, nine-insignia recipient, and holder of ten added commanderies—the full weight of chief minister.

sentences.chinese: 遵至安陽亭，張豺懼而出迎，遵命執之。
sentences.literal: When Zun reached Anyang pavilion, Zhang Chao feared and came out to welcome him; Zun ordered him seized.
sentences.idiomatic: At Anyang pavilion Zhang Chao crept out to greet Shi Zun, who had him arrested on the spot.

sentences.chinese: 於是貫甲曜兵，入自鳳陽門，升于太武前殿，擗踴盡哀，退如東閣。
sentences.literal: Thereupon they donned armor and displayed weapons, entered by Fengyang Gate, ascended the Grand Martial front hall, beat their breasts and stamped in full mourning, then withdrew to the eastern gallery.
sentences.idiomatic: Armored and banners blazing, they entered through Fengyang Gate, climbed the Grand Martial hall to keen and drum their grief, then retired to the eastern wing.

sentences.chinese: 斬張豺于平樂市，夷其三族。
sentences.literal: Zhang Chao was beheaded at Pingle market; his three clans were exterminated.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Chao died on Pingle market scaffold, his three kinships extirpated.

sentences.chinese: 假劉氏令曰：「嗣子幼沖，先帝私恩所授，皇業至重，非所克堪。
sentences.literal: Forging Lady Liu's order it said: "The heir is young and tender; he was appointed by the late emperor's private favor; the imperial enterprise is supremely weighty—not what he can bear.
sentences.idiomatic: A forged rescript in Liu's voice read, "The boy was enthroned by a father's whim; the mandate is too vast for him.

sentences.chinese: 其以遵嗣位。
sentences.literal: Let Zun succeed to the throne."
sentences.idiomatic: Let Shi Zun inherit the throne."

sentences.chinese: 」遵偽讓至於再三，群臣敦勸，乃受之，僭即尊位於太武前殿，大赦殊死已下，罷上白圍。
sentences.literal: Zun falsely declined reaching thrice; the ministers urgently urged; then he accepted, usurped the supreme title at the Grand Martial front hall, granted general amnesty short of capital crimes, and lifted the siege of Shangbai.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Zun thrice refused the crown until his ministers pressed him; then he seized the throne in the Grand Martial hall, amnested all but capital crimes, and raised the siege of Shangbai.

sentences.chinese: 封世為譙王，邑萬戶待以不臣之禮，廢劉氏為太妃，尋皆殺之。
sentences.literal: He enfeoffed Shi as Prince of Qiao with ten thousand households and treated him with the rites due one who is not a subject; he demoted Lady Liu to senior consort; before long both were killed.
sentences.idiomatic: He made Shi Shi prince of Qiao with a ten-thousand-household fief yet honored him like a peer, reduced Lady Liu to senior consort, and soon murdered them both.

sentences.chinese: 世凡立三十三日。
sentences.literal: Shi had altogether occupied the position thirty-three days.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Shi had ruled thirty-three days in all.

sentences.chinese: 石遵
sentences.literal: Shi Zun.
sentences.idiomatic: Section heading: Shi Zun.

sentences.chinese: 於是李農歸請罪，遵復其位，待之如初。
sentences.literal: Thereupon Li Nong returned to ask forgiveness; Zun restored his position and treated him as at first.
sentences.idiomatic: Li Nong came back to plead guilt; Shi Zun restored his offices and favored him as before.

sentences.chinese: 尊其母鄭氏為皇太后，其妻張氏為皇后，以石斌子衍為皇太子，石鑒為侍中，石沖為太保，石苞為大司馬，石琨為大將軍，石閔為中外諸軍事、輔國大將軍、錄尚書事，輔政。
sentences.literal: He honored his mother Lady Zheng as empress dowager, his wife Lady Zhang as empress, appointed Shi Bin's son Yan as crown prince, Shi Jian as attendant-in-chief, Shi Chong as grand guardian, Shi Bao as grand marshal, Shi Kun as grand general, Shi Min as overseer of all military affairs within and without, grand general who aids the state, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, assisting rule.
sentences.idiomatic: He raised Lady Zheng to empress dowager, Lady Zhang to empress, named Shi Yan—Shi Bin's son—heir apparent, Shi Jian palace attendant, Shi Chong grand guardian, Shi Bao grand marshal, Shi Kun commander-in-chief, and Shi Min supreme military overseer, state-aiding grand general, and secretariat regent.

sentences.chinese: 暴風拔樹，震雷，雨雹大如盂升。
sentences.literal: A violent wind uprooted trees; shaking thunder; hail fell as large as bowls and sheng-measures.
sentences.idiomatic: Gales tore up timber, thunder cracked, and hailstones wide as bowls hammered the capital.

sentences.chinese: 太武、暉華殿災，諸門觀閣蕩然，其乘輿服御燒者太半，光焰照天，金石皆盡，火月餘乃滅。
sentences.literal: Grand Martial and Huihua halls suffered fire disaster; gates, towers, and galleries were swept bare; of imperial carriages and wardrobe those burned were more than half; light and flame illumined heaven; metal and stone were all consumed; the fire after more than a month then died.
sentences.idiomatic: Flames gutted the Grand Martial and Huihua halls, stripped gates and belvederes bare, and consumed more than half the chariots and robes—molten metal glared skyward for over a month before the blaze died.

sentences.chinese: 雨血周遍鄴城。
sentences.literal: Blood rain fell everywhere throughout Ye city.
sentences.idiomatic: Rain the color of blood drenched every ward of Ye.

sentences.chinese: 石沖時鎮于薊，聞遵殺世而自立，乃謂其僚佐曰：「世受先帝之命，遵輒廢殺，罪逆莫大，其敕內外戎嚴，孤將親討之。
sentences.literal: Shi Chong at that time was stationed at Ji; hearing Zun had killed Shi and established himself, he said to his staff and aides: "Shi received the late emperor's mandate; Zun abruptly deposed and killed him—the crime of rebellion is greatest; order inner and outer to tighten armor; I myself will personally punish him."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Chong held Ji when news came that Shi Zun had murdered Shi Shi and seized power; he told his advisers, "The boy bore the late emperor's charge—Shi Zun slew him by treason; seal the passes—I march myself to punish him."

sentences.chinese: 」於是留寧北沭堅戍幽州，帥眾五萬，自薊討遵，傳檄燕、趙，所在雲集，比及常山，眾十餘萬。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he left northern pacification Mu Jian to garrison Youzhou, led a host of fifty thousand, from Ji punished Zun, transmitted proclamations through Yan and Zhao; wherever they went clouds gathered; by the time they reached Changshan, the host exceeded one hundred thousand.
sentences.idiomatic: He left Mu Jian of northern pacification to hold Youzhou, took fifty thousand men from Ji, broadcast manifestos across Yan and Zhao until recruits swarmed in—beyond Changshan his army topped a hundred thousand.

sentences.chinese: 次於苑鄉，遇遵赦書，謂左右曰：「吾弟一也，死者不可復追，何為復相殘乎！
sentences.literal: He halted at Yuanxiang; encountering Zun's amnesty edict, he said to those at his side: "My younger brother and I are one; the dead cannot be pursued back—why again mutually injure one another!
sentences.idiomatic: Camped at Yuanxiang, he read Shi Zun's pardon and mused aloud, "He is still my brother—the dead cannot return; why cut one another down again?

sentences.chinese: 吾將歸矣。
sentences.literal: I shall return."
sentences.idiomatic: I am going home."

sentences.chinese: 」其將陳暹進曰：「彭城篡弑自尊，為罪大矣。
sentences.literal: " His general Chen Xian advanced saying: "The prince of Pengcheng usurped and murdered to honor himself—the crime is great.
sentences.idiomatic: General Chen Xian cut in, "The prince of Pengcheng murdered his way to the throne—the guilt is monstrous.

sentences.chinese: 王雖北旆，臣將南轅，平京師，擒彭城，然後奉迎大駕。
sentences.literal: Though Your Highness turns the banner north, your servant will turn the axle south, pacify the capital, capture the prince of Pengcheng, then welcome the great chariot."
sentences.idiomatic: You may wheel north, my lord, but I will drive south, seize the capital, cage the prince of Pengcheng, and only then escort your majesty home."

sentences.chinese: 」沖從之。
sentences.literal: " Chong followed this.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Chong agreed.

sentences.chinese: 遵馳遣王擢以書喻沖，沖弗聽。
sentences.literal: Zun urgently sent Wang Zhuo with a letter to enlighten Chong; Chong did not listen.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Zun raced Wang Zhuo ahead with a letter dissuading Shi Chong, who ignored it.

sentences.chinese: 遵假石閔黃鉞、金鉦，與李農等率精卒十萬討之。
sentences.literal: Zun lent Shi Min the yellow battle-axe and golden cymbals; together with Li Nong and others he led one hundred thousand elite troops to punish him.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Zun handed Shi Min the yellow axe and golden bells; with Li Nong and others he marched one hundred thousand picked troops against the rebel.

sentences.chinese: 戰于平棘，沖師大敗，獲沖於元氏，賜死，坑其士卒三萬餘人。
sentences.literal: They fought at Pingji; Chong's army was greatly defeated; Chong was captured at Yuanshi, granted death, and more than thirty thousand of his soldiers were buried alive in pits.
sentences.idiomatic: At Pingji Shi Chong's host shattered; taken at Yuanshi he was forced to kill himself, and thirty thousand of his men were buried alive in mass graves.

sentences.chinese: 始葬季龍，號其墓為顯原陵，偽諡武皇帝，廟號太祖。
sentences.literal: They began burying Jilong; his tomb was titled Manifest Plain Mound; false posthumous title Martial Emperor; temple name Taizu.
sentences.idiomatic: They laid Shi Hu to rest on Manifest Plain tumulus, posthumously dubbing him Martial Emperor with temple name Taizu.

sentences.chinese: 遵揚州刺史王浹以淮南歸順。
sentences.literal: Zun's Yangzhou Governor Wang Jie brought Huainan to allegiance in surrender.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Zun's Yangzhou governor Wang Jie delivered Huainan to Jin in submission.
